title: Adversarial Signed Graph Learning with Differential Privacy

problem.claim: Training signed graph learning models on sensitive signed graphs can leak private link information through model parameters.

gap.claim: Existing differential-privacy methods for unsigned graphs are not well-suited to signed graphs because edge perturbation can cause cascading sign-inference errors and gradient perturbation can require substantial noise due to higher gradient sensitivity.

contributions.claim: ASGL is a privacy-preserving adversarial signed graph learning method designed to preserve utility while achieving node-level differential privacy.
ASGL separates signed graphs into positive and negative subgraphs and uses a gradient-perturbed adversarial module to approximate the true signed connectivity distribution.
ASGL uses a constrained breadth-first search tree strategy combined with balance theory to identify edge signs between generated node pairs and enable gradient decoupling.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that ASGL achieves favorable privacy-utility trade-offs across multiple downstream tasks on real-world datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Signed graphs represent complex relationships with positive and negative edges, and signed graph learning can preserve structural and sign information in node embeddings.
Privacy risks arise because model parameters trained on sensitive signed graphs may leak private link information.
Existing differential-privacy approaches for unsigned graphs face cascading sign-inference errors or high gradient sensitivity when applied to signed graphs.
ASGL combines subgraph separation, adversarial gradient perturbation, and a constrained breadth-first search strategy integrated with balance theory.
Experiments on real-world datasets report favorable privacy-utility trade-offs across multiple downstream tasks.

source_observation.claim: The constrained breadth-first search strategy enables gradient decoupling and is reported to lower gradient sensitivity.

interpretation.claim: Constraining the dependency structure used for sign inference may reduce interdependence in privacy-sensitive gradient computation.

application.claim: When multi-hop relational inference increases gradient sensitivity, use constrained traversal structures to limit dependency coupling.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the constraints, computational cost, or failure cases of the breadth-first search strategy.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide privacy-budget values or quantitative utility results.
The abstract does not identify the datasets, downstream tasks, baselines, or experimental protocol.
The abstract does not specify the formal node-level differential-privacy guarantee.
